title: SHA-256 PoW on Intel Iris Xe (gen12lp) through OpenCL NEO and IGC

host.gpu: Intel Iris(R) Xe Graphics (ADL-P, gen12lp, 96 EUs)

kernel: tools/xe-sha256-opencl.c: one work-item per nonce, nonce in W[0], 48-byte message, clz hit test
notes: First native Intel GPU measurement here. Level Zero has no driver on this machine (only the loader); OpenCL does, so this goes through NEO and IGC. The hand-written listing in src/intel/xe is not executed: it is verified by interpreting its own instruction list and by assembling with IGA.

library_backend.entry: anubis_opencl_solve() called from anubis_solve_bits() and anubis_solve_nibbles()
library_backend.dispatch_order: CUDA -> Level Zero -> Vulkan -> OpenCL -> CPU
library_backend.enabled_by: ANUBIS_OPENCL=1, or no other GPU backend answering
library_backend.kernel: src/opencl/sha256_pow.cl, one work-item per nonce, 64 lanes per workgroup
library_backend.partial_prefix: pre[]/pre_len carry the leftover bytes of a 32-byte Anubis randomData; keeps whole-block folded state in mid[]
library_backend.verified: every hit re-verified by anubis_verify_bits/anubis_verify_nibbles before being accepted

library_throughput_mhps.note: measured with difficulty 63 so no hit ends the search early; the first dispatch after idle is slow while the GPU clocks up

end_to_end.gate: betterAnusbis --algorithm sha256 --difficulty 26 (Anubis-compatible, same JSON and cookie)
end_to_end.speedup: 12x to 39x in wall time, 13.4x in hashes/s
end_to_end.cpu_condition: four threads (the CLI default), powersave governor at 1.2 GHz; a single thread measures 5.0-5.6 MH/s in tools/bench_gpu.py

bugs_found_while_wiring: p_clCreateBuffer was declared (ctx, flags_as_ulong, size_as_int, host, err) and every call site passed size then flags, so no device buffer was ever created and every search returned 'exhausted' without hashing
the dispatch used local size 1 (one lane per workgroup) and a blocking transfer per chunk: 14 MH/s before, ~285 MH/s after 64-lane workgroups and one results write per search
an OpenCL device that reports itself as a CPU (pocl) is now refused instead of silently beating the AVX2 code by being slower
kernel_bug_hypothesis_rejected: an early guess blamed IGC for miscompiling the local digest array in the hit test; reverting that rewrite kept the kernel correct, so the cause was the host buffers, not the compiler

bench_gpu_rows_2026_11_13.note: tools/bench_gpu.py; the 'level zero' row is the OpenCL fallback because Level Zero is not compiled in on this machine (no level_zero/ze_api.h), and short workloads pay the cold first dispatch
